summary: Obfuscated credential stealer disguised as a CSS utility
details: birch-css-utils@1.2.2 advertises itself as a tiny zero-dependency CSS token-blending helper, but its `main` entry (`index.mjs`) and two sibling modules (`build-cache.mjs`, `cache-sweep.mjs`) are heavily obfuscated bundles totaling roughly 760 KB, each prefixed with fabricated 'Auto-generated by <unrelated-package>' banners and built around obfuscator.io-style base64+XOR string arrays using different keys per file. Decoded string fragments from `index.mjs` include AWS STS response identifiers such as `getCallerIdentity`, user-profile directory names (`localappdata`, `appdata`, `home`), and tokens such as `authorized`, `post`, `git`, `email` — none of which have any role in CSS token manipulation and are characteristic of a cloud-credential and local-profile harvester that runs at `require()`/`import` time. The published manifest's `files` array also lists `cache-warm.mjs`, which is absent from the tarball, indicating the artifact was assembled outside a normal build. The cover-story README, mismatched banners, per-file XOR keys, and credential-shaped decoded strings together constitute an installer-side credential-theft payload masquerading as a utility library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
